tryOnView.fitMatchInfoCalibrated: We compare the brand's size chart with your body measurements from the photo. The benchmark is how the brand itself wears this piece: their model is {$height} cm tall and wears size {$size}. The closer this size comes to that look on your body, the higher the score. Running tight costs far more than running loose. Off lengths lower the score slightly but never change the size recommendation.
tryOnView.fitMatchInfoDerived: This chart wasn't published by the brand. We measured the garment's own pattern across its sizes and compared those measurements with your body measurements from the photo. The numbers are exact, but the intended fit (how loose the brand means it to wear) is our estimate, so treat the recommendation as a strong starting point.
tryOnView.sameAcrossSizes: This measurement barely differs between sizes. Picking another size won't change it much.
tryOnView.metricInfo.chest: Chest width: how much room the garment has around the chest compared to your chest measurement.
tryOnView.metricInfo.waist: Waist width: the garment's girth at the waist compared to your waist measurement.
tryOnView.metricInfo.totalLength: Total length: where the hem ends on you, measured against the length the cut intends.
tryOnView.metricInfo.sleeveLength: Sleeve length: where the cuff ends on you, measured against the intended sleeve length.
tryOnView.metricInfo.other: This measurement of the garment compared to your body.
tryOnView.metricGirthDelta: In this size: {$cm} cm of room versus your body measurement (+ = more ease).
tryOnView.metricLengthDelta: In this size: {$cm} cm versus the intended length (+ = longer).
tryOnView.fitMatchInfo: We compare the brand's size chart with your body measurements from the photo. The key girth (e.g. chest) drives the score: how close is the garment's ease to what the cut intends? Deviations cost points, and running tight costs far more than running loose. Off lengths lower the score slightly but never change the size recommendation.
